<a id="overview"></a>

## Overview

A procedure is a folder: its ddoc, its rendering (the human how-to), and anything only it uses, including its own justfile. A project's procedures live in `docs/project/procedures/<area>/`; those that ship to every project live in `skills/pij/procedures/<area>/`. One runner, `skills/pij/tools/procedures/procedures.ts`, reads the documents and runs steps as `just` recipes, checking inputs, order and preconditions first and a done check after, and records progress in a git-ignored file per checkout. It also books ids through `pij claim`, lists procedures, records status changes through ddocs, and holds the drift check that harness checks runs. It adds no loop, poll, timer or hook: it runs only when a seat or the gate calls it.

<a id="decisions"></a>

## Decisions

| id | decision | why | realises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d-1 | The runner is one TypeScript file in the skill, run by node's type stripping, with no build and no dependencies. | It then works in any repo where pij is installed, as pr-freeze does, and needs no daemon or Rust change. The shim can load it in-process. | [req-08](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-30](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-2 | No import line in the root justfile: the runner runs each procedure's own justfile directly. | The survey's name clashes and swallowed flags came from area modules sharing the root namespace; this removes both and keeps deleting the folder a complete removal. | [req-04](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-07](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-15](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-3 | Numbers are booked with the existing claim kinds `procedure-&lt;area&gt;`. | `pij claim` already takes any lowercase kind with one ledger and never reuses a number, and #342 finds folders in any case. Per-area numbers give the ids the PRD names (PROC-meta-0001). The runner guards the one gap: a folder that already holds the number. | [req-02](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-4 | Preconditions and done checks are recipes: exit 0 passes. Order checks run the other step's done check first and use recorded progress only when it has none. | Recipes are what seats already run, so no predicate language is needed (non-goal n-1), and live state is right when the other step ran in another checkout (osk-central's review). | [req-11](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-12](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-5 | A decision step refuses until recorded; nothing waits. | Waiting needs a poll or a hook, which req-28 forbids. | [req-17](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-28](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-6 | Listing never runs a check; it reads progress. | Listing is the most frequent call; it must cost nothing (req-28). | [req-14](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-28](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-7 | Co-location is a report, not a gate. | The operator's ruling of 2026-11-24: a file used by one procedure today may be shared tomorrow. | [req-06](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |
| d-8 | An area lives in one home; the skill's areas are reserved elsewhere. | Every project books its own numbers, so a project's PROC-meta-0001 would collide with the skill's. | [req-02](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements), [req-03](../prds/005-procedures.dd.md#requirements) |

| k-5 | `proc new` and `proc status`. | on demand: one `pij claim` request (the daemon scans in-process), a few git calls, and ddocs validate, set and build per document | per procedure written or approved | [c-booking](#components), [c-status](#components) |
